paras.text: Credit Creation
paras.urdu: اعتباری زر کی تخلیق (Credit Creation)
paras.pashto: د اعتباري پیسو پیدا کول (Credit Creation)

paras.text: When some person asks the bank for a loan and the bank, after taking security etc., becomes ready to give the loan, it does not give that person cash rupees; rather it merely enters in its account books, in his name, notionally that “this much money of yours has been deposited with the bank as a trust”, and giving him a cheque book directs him that he should not withdraw cash now, but rather give a cheque of the particular sum to the one whom he has to pay. The one receiving the cheque deposits this cheque in his account in the same bank. As it were, that cheque comes back again to the same bank, and the bank does not need to give cash rupees. This is called creating money. Because the bank, instead of issuing cash rupees, created a notional “deposit” with itself which, for the customer, is exactly equal to cash rupees. The creation of this deposit is “creation of money”.

اعتباری زر کی تخلیق (Credit Creation)

جب کوئی شخص بینک سے قرضہ مانگے اور بینک ضمانت وغیرہ لے کر قرضہ دینے پر آمادہ ہو جائے تو یہ نہیں کرتا کہ اس شخص کو نقد روپیہ دے دے، بلکہ اپنے بہی کھاتوں میں اس کے نام کے آگے فرضی طور پر یہ درج کر لیتا ہے۔ کہ تمہارا اتنا پیسہ امانت کے طور پر بینک میں جمع ہے اور اسے چیک بک دے کر یہ ہدایت کرتا ہے کہ چیک اسی وقت نقد روپیہ نکلوائے۔ بلکہ اس نے جس کو ادائیگی کرنی ہوتی ہے۔ اسے مخصوص رقم کا چیک دے دیتا ہے۔ چیک وصول کرنے والا اس چیک کو اسی بینک میں اپنے حساب میں جمع کروا دیتا ہے۔ گویا وہ چیک دوبارہ اسی بینک کے پاس آ جاتا ہے۔ اور بینک کو نقد روپیہ دینے کی ضرورت نہیں پڑتی اسے زر پیدا کرنا کہتے ہیں۔ کیونکہ بینک نے نقد روپیہ جاری کرنے کی بجائے اپنے پاس ایک فرضی ”امانت“ پیدا کر لی جو گاہک کے لیے بالکل نقد روپیہ کے برابر رہی ہے۔ اسی امانت کی تخلیق ”زر کی تخلیق“ ہے۔

زر کس طرح تخلیق کیا جاتا ہے؟ (How Credit is Created)

اوپر بیان کیا کہ تجارتی بینک قرضہ دے کر اعتباری زر کے پھیلاؤ کی معرفت زر تخلیق کر لیتے ہیں۔ یہاں ہم اس مسئلہ پر بحث کرتے ہیں کہ بینک کس طرح اور کتنا زر تخلیق کر سکتے ہیں اس کی وضاحت کے لیے تین باتیں فرض کرتے ہیں۔

مفروضات (Assumptions)

i۔ پہلی بات یہ کہ ہر بینک قانونی طور پر اس بات کا پابند ہے کہ وہ اپنے کل واجبات کا پچیس فیصد نقد زر کی شکل میں اپنے پاس رکھے۔ واجبات سے مراد وہ رقوم ہیں۔ جو بینک کے اوپر واجب الادا ہوں یعنی لوگوں کی امانتیں وغیرہ۔

ii۔ دوسرا مفروضہ یہ ہے کہ تمام ادائیگیاں اور وصولیاں چیکوں کی معرفت ہوتی ہے نقد شکل میں نہیں۔

iii۔ تیسرا مفروضہ یہ ہے کہ کسی ایک بینک میں کوئی شخص چار سو روپے کی نئی امانت جمع کرواتا ہے۔

پہلے ہم صرف یہ دیکھتے ہیں کہ کوئی ایک بینک کس طرح اور کتنا زر تخلیق کرتا ہے اور پھر یہ دیکھیں گے کہ پورے ملک میں اجتماعی طور پر سارے بینک مل کر کتنی مقدار میں زر تخلیق کر سکتے ہیں۔

بینک کے پاس جمع کرائے گئے 400 روپوں میں سے 300 روپے بینک نے بطور قرض جاری کر دیئے ہیں۔ یہ رقم قرض لینے والے … (ص 51 پر جاری)

Credit Creation

When some person asks the bank for a loan and the bank, after taking security etc., becomes ready to give the loan, it does not give that person cash rupees; rather it merely enters in its account books, in his name, notionally that “this much money of yours has been deposited with the bank as a trust”, and giving him a cheque book directs him that he should not withdraw cash now, but rather give a cheque of the particular sum to the one whom he has to pay. The one receiving the cheque deposits this cheque in his account in the same bank. As it were, that cheque comes back again to the same bank, and the bank does not need to give cash rupees. This is called creating money. Because the bank, instead of issuing cash rupees, created a notional “deposit” with itself which, for the customer, is exactly equal to cash rupees. The creation of this deposit is “creation of money”.

How is credit created? (How Credit is Created)

It was stated above that commercial banks, by giving loans, create money through the expansion of credit money. Here we discuss this problem how banks can create money and how much money. For its explanation we assume three things.

Assumptions

i. The first thing is that every bank is legally bound to keep twenty-five per cent of its total liabilities with it in the form of cash. Liabilities mean those sums which are payable by the bank, i.e. the deposits of people etc.

ii. The second assumption is that all payments and receipts take place through cheques, not in cash form.

iii. The third assumption is that in some one bank some person deposits a new deposit of four hundred rupees.

First we only see how and how much money one bank creates, and then we will see in what quantity all banks together in the whole country can create money collectively.

Credit creation by a single bank (Credit Creation by Single Bank)

Suppose that a person deposits four hundred rupees as a deposit with some bank. From this, on one side the assets or receivable sums of the bank will increase by four hundred rupees. Assets mean those sums which are the property of the bank; and on the other side its liabilities, i.e. payable sums, will increase by four hundred rupees, because ultimately this deposited sum will have to be paid back to the depositor. The bank will not be able to keep this sum with it in cash form, because it is legally bound to keep only twenty-five per cent in cash. Therefore, keeping one hundred rupees cash, it will lend the remaining three hundred rupees on interest to a needy trader. Its balance sheet (Balance Sheet) will take the following form.

Collective credit creation by all banks (Credit Creation by Whole Bankeing System)

It has been told above that one bank keeps 25% of the deposit deposited with it and lends the rest. But it is evident that the borrower will pay this sum by cheque to the one to whom he pays, and this sum will be transferred into his account, from which the deposits with their banks will increase. Every bank, keeping 25% of these deposits with it, will issue the remaining sum as a loan. In this way this chain will go on continuously, and the total loan will become many times more than the original deposit. Its explanation has been given in the following table.
